:::{#thm-proof-by-contradiction}
#### A proof by contradiction proves its proposition

Let $P$ and $Q$ be propositions (@def-proposition).
If $\neg P \Rightarrow Q$ is true and $Q$ is false, then $P$ is true.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

::: proof

By @def-implies, $\neg P \Rightarrow Q$ is false only when $\neg P$ is true and $Q$ is false.
Here $Q$ is false, and $\neg P \Rightarrow Q$ is true,
so $\neg P$ is not true.
Then $\neg P$ is false.
Since $\neg P$ is true whenever $P$ is false,
$P$ must be true.

:::

:::
